title.narrative: Diakonia - HR and Governance Program fas II
Diakonia - HR and Governance Program phase II

description.narrative:
Detta är den andra fasen av Demokrati och Mänskliga Rättigheter-programmet, planerat att genomföras mellan den 1 juli 2018 till den 30 juni 2021. Budgeten planeras till 75 MSEK. Den första fasen genomfördes mellan 1 juli 2015 till den 31 juli 2018, efter en förlängning (no-cost) från det ursprungliga planerade slutdatumet vid 2017 års slut. Förlängningen orsakades huvudsakligen av val och omval 2017 vilka orsakade att implementeringen tog längre tid än planerat. Programmet kommer att fortsätta arbetet som påbörjades under den första fasen. Resultat från den utvärdering som genomfördes i slutet av 2017 har använts för att förändra programmet och en ny partner inkluderas. Fler counties (län) och nya komponenter införlivas, bl.a. engagemang i the Kenya we want och Building bridges-initiativen.
Programmet kom ursprungligen till för att komplettera ambassadens institutionella stöd i Kenya mot samma mål genom civilsamhällets engagemang. Trots att vissa av ambassadens stöd har upphört (polisen) har Diakonia valt att fortsätta ansträngningarna som man lade ner i första fasen, för att bygga på det man uppnått under fas I. Baserat på de svårigheter som rådde i arbetet med institutionsstödet till polisen, kopplat till det alltjämt centrala behoven av att reformera polisen, stöder ambassaden valet att inkludera detta i fas II av programmet.
Programmet har två huvudresultat: 1. 'Strengthened accountability and independence of governance structures and institutions at local and national level', med fem underliggande resultat. Fokus ligger på ansvarstagarna. 2.'Inclusive, cohesive and accountable society through increased citizen engagement in governance process.' Det andra resultatet har tre underliggande resultat och fukuserar på rättighetsinnehavarna.
Vad gäller ansvarstagarna i programmet, kommer man, som nämnts, fortsätta arbeta med polisen, främst genom att stärka närpolisens kommitteer och s.k. Community Policing Forums på polisstationsnivå. Inom rättssystemet fortsätter man implementeringen av alternativa rättssystem, driver på implementering av policies som etablerades under fas I. Riksåklagaren och kriminalvården kommer att få kapacitetsstöd. De oberoende nationella kommissionerna kommer att stärkas som en del av tillhandahållande av tjänster för medborgarna i det fortsatta förändringsarbetet.
För rättighetsinnehavarna kommer programmet att stärka deltagande på länsnivå, liksom stödja medborgarna att hålla ansvariga till svars, liksom att begära förbättringar vad gäller den ekonomiska förvaltningen och tjänster som de har rätt att åtnjuta. Civilsamhället kommer också att stödjas att fortsätta sitt påverkansarbete för ett gynnsamt klimat för civilt manöverutrymme. Följden av 2017 års val blev ett alltmer polariserat land och programmet kommer adressera behovet av sammanhållning genom att bygga på det nationella initiativet the "Kenya we want" och främja dialog för att ena landet.
Diakonia är en organisation baserad på kristna värderinga som arbetar med runt 350 organisationer i 25 länder. Organisationen ämnar att arbeta för en rättivs, jämlik och varaktigt förändrad värld, fri från fattigdom, förtryck, ojämlikhet och våld. Diakonia utför inte egna projekt, utan stödjer lokala partnerorganisationer. Man får ekonomisk finansiering från individer och församlingar i Sverige, liksom institutionellt stöd från Sida, ambassader, EU och andra internationella organisationer.

This is the second phase of the Democracy and Human Rights Program, planned to be implemented from the 1st of July 2018 to the 30th of June 2021, with a planned budget of 75 MSEK. The first phase was carried out between the 1st of July 2015 to the 31st of July 2018, after a no cost extension from the originally planned end at the end of 2017. The no cost extension was to a large extent caused by the 2017 elections which slowed down implementation of the program. The program will continue with the work that started during the first phase, taking into account the findings of the midterm evaluation that was carried out at the end of 2017 and address those through amending and include a new partner and increase in county presence and new components; among others to engage in the Kenya we want and Building bridges initiatives.
The program came about as a way for the Embassy to complement the institutional support in Kenya with efforts towards the same through civil society engagement. Although some of the Embassy´s institutional support have ended (police), Diakonia has chosen to continue the efforts made so far on the civil society level, to leverage on gains made during phase I. Given the difficulties experienced working directly with the police, but the critical need to reform the institution, the Embassy supports the choice to include these efforts in phase II.
The program has two main outcomes: 1. 'Strengthened accountability and independence of governance structures and institutions at local and national level', with five intermediate outcomes. This outcome focuses on the duty bearers. 2.'Inclusive, cohesive and accountable society through increased citizen engagement in governance process.' The second outcome has three intermediate outcomes and is focusing on the rights holders.
On the duty bearer side the program will, as previously mentioned, continue working with the police, mainly strengthening Community Policing Committees and Community Policing Forums at the police station levels. The work with the Judiciary will continue the implementation of Alternative Justice Systems (AJS), pushing the implementation of policies that were established during the first phase. Capacity building of the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) and the Prisons will continue. The work with the Independent commissions will be strengthened as parts of the supply side of the change continuum.
On the demand side, the program will strengthen public participation at county level, as well as supporting citizens to demand accountability and improvements in public financial management and service delivery. Civil society will also be supported to continue their advocacy for improved environment for civic action. The 2017 elections left an increasingly divided country behind and the program will address the need for cohesion through building on the national framework of the "Kenya we want" and foster dialogue aiming at moving the country towards reconciliation.
Diakonia is a faith-based Swedish development organisation working with around 350 local organisations in about 25 countries. The organisation aims to work for a just, equal and sustainable world free from poverty, oppression, inequality and violence. Diakonia does not carry out projects on their own, but instead supports local partner organisations. Its funding comes from donations by individuals and congregations in Sweden, as well as institutional funding from Sida, embassies, the EU and other international organisations.

The Program strives to achieve a 'Strengthened democratic culture through accountable and independent governance structures and institutions at local and national level' as well as 'Inclusive, cohesive and accountable society throught increased citizen engagement in governance processes'.

Outcome 1: Strengthened democratic culture through accountable and independent governance structres and institutions at local and national level
The completion of water projects that had stalled in Baringo County leading to access to water to an estimated population of 100,000 was due to improved capacity of budget practitioners in the County to factor in citizen requests.
There were actions by the Attorney General and the Cabinet Secretary following the Public Interest Litigation (PIL) on the right to access information about health care, focusing on the governments handling of the COVID-19 pandemic by Katiba Institute. These include investigations and prosecutions and publicizing of details of irregularities in the award of KEMSA tenders. The PIL also contributed to increased public awareness, including media focus on the need for the government to be accountable to Kenyans in its management of COVID-19, including respecting rights of Kenyans to information.
Greater duty bearer responsiveness was witnessed in the increase in the National Police Services (NPS) Internal Affairs Units (IAU) accountability channels as a result of Transparency International Kenyas support for a robust Anonymous Reporting Information System (ARIS). The unit is now fully maintained having been assigned an operational budget by the ministry of Interior and Coordination of National Government and offering citizens an avenue for anonymous reporting.
The Program support of the Police Reforms Working Group (PRWG) resulted in policy-level outcomes such as the MOU to develop a clear framework for engagement on policing issues. Towards this, the Police Reforms Working Group (PRWG) successfully lobbied for abandonment of proposed amendments to reform the security sector which sought to transform the National Police Service Commission (NPSC) into a National Police Council (NPC) which would have materially watered-down gains in the sector.
Prisons were decongested as a result of the support for Alternative Justice System where cumulatively, the elders resolved over one thousand, five hundred (1,500) cases since its introduction in prisons.
The support to FIDA Kenya enabled the screening of over ten thousand (10,000) cases out of which one thousand, six hundred and eighteen (1,618) women cases were filed in court between 2018-2022.
Strategic litigation/ advocacy actions towards LGBTQ rights through support to the National Gay and Lesbian Human Rights Commission (NGLHRC) led to a raft of Judicial pronouncements that affirm SOGIE-SC rights.
There was also a 60% increase in the number of LGBTIQ persons who benefited from pro bono legal aid services on SOCIESC-related violations.
Outcome 2: Inclusive, cohesive, and accountable society through increased citizen engagement in governance processes
A total of 310 budget cafes were held over the period of implementation which significantly contributed to more citizens proactively engaging in the budget process by presenting their concerns and priorities. These citizen actions contributed to the responsiveness of duty bearers reported in outcome 1.
Enhanced cross-county synergy in Public Finance Accountability was achieved leading to the establishment of regional budget hubs in which budget transparency surveys were introduced. The surveys led to a marked increase in transparency as observed in the counties availing more information to the public. The Coast budget hub for example conducted a coordinated access to information campaign which saw the counties in Coast region publishing more budget documents on their websites.
The goal of having more than 30% of all the service delivery issues raised in the forums at different levels responded to by duty bearers was realized in Uasin Gishu, Nakuru, Garissa, Baringo, Bungoma, Busia, Isiolo and Mombasa Counties. Citizens reported greater satisfaction with service delivery in some of the targeted areas hence affirming the outcomes of their engagement that came from their strengthened capacity to engage.
A further demonstration of greater capacity was in the affirmative action of having more persons with disabilities, women and youth engage in budget and other processes. IBP working with County partners supported more women and persons with disabilities (PWDs) to engage in budgets through having their specific participation in the budget cafés and distinctly raising issues affecting them. They addressed challenges around allocation and disbursement of social protection funds for persons with disabilities and challenges of underfunding of social sectors that often affect the livelihoods of women such as water and health that take significant time as women take care for their families.
IRCK established interfaith women and Youth Networks in the counties of Isiolo, Mombasa and Baringo which processed and issued a total of 25 petitions to 3 county governments and engaged on a myriad of issues including insecurity, interethnic conflict, Female Genital Mutilation among others.
The engagement of faith actors in national cohesion and integration processes bore fruit with the successful shuttle diplomacy during the tense presidential vote tallying and announcement in the 2022 general election. Peace was maintained, and a smooth transition realized.
Following advocacy and follow-up by right holders was the success in efforts to eradicate statelessness in Kenya. The Kenya Human Rights Commission diligently continued to advocate for the timely release of citizenship certificates for the Shona community submitted in November 2020. This effort culminated in the Ministry of Interior signing one thousand and seven (1,007) citizenship certificates in May 2021, and six hundred and fifty-three (653) remaining ones in June 2021 ending the protracted journey to recognition of the Shona community in Kenya.
Further, a total of three hundred and ninety six (396) members of the Rwandese community from Kericho, Nandi, Bomet, Kisii, Nyeri, Kiambu counties were supported to fill requisite forms and submit citizenship application forms to the National Taskforce on Statelessness for review and vetting.
Over the course of four years, the Program to a large extent met its objectives as envisioned in the two outcome areas and therefore can attribute its contribution to changes in observed in the country. As such, the state, and its agencies, both at national and county levels have exhibited improved transparency, better accountability and inclusion in service delivery as demonstrated by the various indicators. The program has also largely helped strengthen capacities of agencies, thus leveraging on capacities in order to enhance service delivery to the people. The agencies which were targeted through the program actions have demonstrated improved capacity in responding to their mandate.
The program successfully engaged with various stakeholders, including government bodies, civil society organizations, local communities, and marginalized groups. Through facilitating dialogue, capacity-strengthening sessions, and advocating for policy reforms, the program played a pivotal role in enhancing the accountability and transparency of governmental institutions. This, in turn, contributed to a more inclusive and participatory democratic process, allowing citizens to have a greater say in matters affecting their lives.
The Evaluation that took place in 2021, confirmed many of the results that had been achieved up to that time.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
